title: Every rep · Say it. To anyone, about any customer.
what: Kevin, 17 Sep, 6:40 PM: "make a video showing how to use this little contact-other-people thing on the mobile app… I don't even know how to use it." The box under the money on the Today tab. Top line: who it's about (type the last name, tap the customer). Big box: say it. POST. With a customer it lands on that customer's file as a team note; @Jessica Coley or @office in the words buzzes them; the customer never sees it. Leave the name blank and it goes to the Village, where everyone with a seat reads it; @sales, @supers, @office buzzes the group. When they answer, your phone buzzes and it's on the same file.
meta: 6 scenes · ~2 minutes · 17 Sep · the phone app, Today tab (312 · 360 · 363) · no switch

title: Every rep · When you miss a call or a text
what: Kevin, 17 Sep, 4:20 PM: "I have the strangest suspicion that we're missing calls and text." We were. The 15-minute "not answered" notice went only to the watcher and to Kevin, never to the rep; a text on a rep's own number never buzzed the app and landed 15 minutes late; and nobody read the phone company's call list, so 50 calls a day rang out with no one the wiser. Tonight: a customer text on your own number buzzes you when it lands (399); the 15-minute clock buzzes you first and skips ratings, STOP, thank-yous and test files (400); every call sits on the customer's file, and a missed call from a customer buzzes you once (401). Robocalls never buzz. Nothing buzzes 7:30 PM–8 AM. A missed call can show up to an hour late: the list comes once an hour.
meta: 5 scenes · ~2 minutes · 17 Sep · migrations 399 + 400 + 401 · Central Command v113 · no switch

title: Mike · The estimate, line by line, in the 4-Touch app
what: Kevin, 17 Sep, 5 PM: "Mike is only on the MVP mobile app… put that same thing inside." The ESTIMATE ON FILE sheet in the app now has A PICTURE / LINE BY LINE: what it is, qty, unit, price each, + ITEM, the total is the project value, SAVE makes the customer's link (the same Billdu-shaped page, one ACCEPT), and Text it now sends it from the Oasis line. And 6 PM: "he can type whatever he wants or he can get the pop-ups" — under WHAT IT IS sits the whole Oasis menu (palms · bushes & shrubs · mulch & rock · flowers · the job, 48 items from the design folder), typing finds matches, a tap fills the name, the unit and the last price used. Published over the air 17 Sep ~6:10 PM (runtime 1.0.4).

title: Mike · Jess · The sub locked in, on the contract picture
what: Kevin and Jess, 17 Sep, the Billdu handoff: Mike gets the sub's number before he prices the job, kept it in a CompanyCam picture, and once it signed emailed Jess the Billdu link, the sub and the amount. Now it is one question on the contract picture (＋ Photo → This picture is the signed contract) or the 🔒 Lock the sub button on the file: who is doing the work, their price, their cell once. The sub is texted the picture and the price from the Oasis line and taps RECIBIDO; Jess is tagged with the sub and the price (her phone, her email, her text); she presses Copy for CC, then Typed into CC, and the Office room lists what is still waiting. Nobody remembers anything. Billdu is untouched today. Narrated (Guy).

title: Jess · Laura · Sam · Monday: every new lead starts here
what: From Mon 21 Sep a new customer comes in through + New lead, not through Contractors Cloud: type it once, pick the rep and the time (the form shows the rep's day), press Open the file. The rep's phone buzzes, the booking is the file's first line, the customer gets the confirmation text when its switch is on, and the machine carries the lead into CC when its switch is on — until then, Copy for CC. Nothing else moves. Later the same day, Samantha's first idea: the Street box suggests the address as you type, and a pick fills street, city and zip; the rep list carries Gio and Jessica beside the sellers. Narrated (Guy).

what: The customer accepts now and signs everything once — the proposal, our contract sheet, the disclosures, the hold harmless, the permit application. Oasis signs the contract alone. The Notice of Commencement is the one form not on the link: it goes to the customer by email to sign in front of a notary, the machine texts them until the picture lands, and the rep never goes back. what: One link signs the job: the proposal and our contract sheet, seven green spots. The disclosures can ride the same link with one switch. The NOC, the Hold Harmless and the permit applications need a notary, so the file fills them in from the county's owner of record and Sam prints, notarizes and pulls the permit. Narrated (Guy), 2:18.
